data.long_meaning: From the Arabic word 'mustahsan', meaning pleasing, satisfying, or one who is pleased with the faith. In Islamic history, Mustahsan is a name given to individuals who were content and satisfied with their faith. The name Mustahsan carries the meaning “Pleasing, Satisfying” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mustahsan usually hope their child will grow to embody pleasing, satisfying and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the name Mustahsan bin Abd al-Haqq as the founder of the Hafsid dynasty in 894 AH (1489 AD) in Tunisia.
historical_references.context: Founding of the Hafsid Dynasty in Tunisia

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi mentions Mustahsan bin Abd al-Haqq as a notable figure during the rule of the Mamluk Sultan Qansuh al-Ghuri (922-930 AH, 1516-1517 AD) in Egypt. He was the governor of Alexandria and played a significant role in the defense against the Ottoman Turks.
historical_references.context: Governor of Alexandria during the Mamluk Period, defending against the Ottoman Turks
